comment: ACTIVITY DATA (v7). Stands in for the household's wearables and the Health app.
WHICH GOAL THIS SERVES: meal_plan, and only meal_plan. It is the evidence behind the
'workout-friendly' PREFERENCE the cloud resolves for a meal goal — the planner reads
the routine here and shapes the week's protein around it. It is soft by nature: a
calorie target that could BLOCK a dinner would be a medical rule, and nobody entered
WHY THERE IS NO WorkoutObserver AND NO workout_routine DOMAIN. An IDomainObserver is
what makes the cloud ADVERTISE a domain, and the interpreter classifies against those
hints — so adding one here would start routing 'help me train for a 10k' to this
device, which cannot advance it. Activity is a FACT the meal planner reasons over, not
a kind of goal the Family Hub can run. MealPlanObserver watches it instead.
WHAT IS AND IS NOT IN HERE. `routine` and `recent` are the STEADY STATE: what this
household normally does, which is what Act 1 plans against. The Act 2 spike (12,400
steps) is deliberately NOT here — it arrives through data/daily_events.json like every
other world change, because the feed is where the materiality decision lives. If the
spike were seeded here it would already be true on day 1 and the adaptation would be
GENERIC CLOCK: `day_offset` is resolved against IClock.Today at READ time, so -1 is
always yesterday, on any day the demo runs.

notes: Rohan is the one who logs; the plan is cooked for the household either way.
Hard days want more protein at dinner; rest days want it lighter.
